lines.note: Continues Na- at the end of f508 to form nagahashi, the long bridge. The horses make a rumbling tread; comamo and todoroto belong to the Japanese example, not the Portuguese gloss.

runs.text: Os caualos que paßauaõ pella ponte comprida

lines.note: Begins the translation of the bridge example: horses were passing along the long bridge. The historical spelling and final-vowel tilde in paßauaõ are retained.

runs.text: de madeira com os pès fazendo traquinada.

lines.note: Completes the example with the wooden bridge and the clattering made by the horses’ feet. Traquinada describes their noise or commotion.
Tǒfa is explained by fumiyaburu, breaking or destroying something by treading on it. The Portuguese verb phrase continues with the feet on the next row.
Com os pès completes the definition: the destruction is done with the feet. This is a genuine short continuation of Tǒfa.
Tôfai is equated with ware to hitoshii tomogara, companions or people of equal standing. The first long-o mark is a circumflex in this entry.
Completes the description of equals as people of the same dignity or rank. Teor belongs to the Portuguese explanation of their common standing.
Tofameki names moving or acting in a flustered manner. The scan reads Modo, correcting OCR Mode; fa- begins fazer on the following row.

runs.text: zer algũa couſa atabalhoadamente, ou cõ per-

lines.note: Completes fazer and describes performing something confusedly or in a flurry. The divided per- continues into perturbação below.
Turbação completes per-turbação, disturbance or confusion. The scan does not support the OCR’s internal word break.
Tofatsuki is assigned the same hurried or flustered sense by Idem. The principal parts remain qu and ita as printed.

Tofatofato suru illustrates acting in that same flustered way. The initial of ſuru is damaged; it lacks the clear projecting crossbar seen in nearby f types. Long ſ is the chosen reading, supported by Japanese morphology and the preceding gloss, but the glyph remains a nonblocking uncertainty.
Tofi juxtaposes the capital and countryside, explained by Qiǒ and inaca and Portuguese corte and aldea. These are paired Japanese glosses rather than Portuguese embedded terms.
Tǒfit is glossed as Tǒ no fude, the Chinese brush or its work; the Portuguese gives painting or writing. The repeated Tǒ has a downward caron in the scan, not the OCR’s circumflex.
China completes the definition of Tǒfit as Chinese painting or writing. It is Portuguese running text and remains italic.
Tofǒ is explained by jippō, ten directions or quarters. The scan has a point after 10; To- starts the example rather than another entry.

runs.text: Não ſaber parte de ſi com tri-

lines.note: Tofǒ wo ushinō means losing one’s bearings or being at a loss. The Portuguese describes not knowing what to do through sadness; tri- continues into tristeza.
Completes tri-steza and starts tofǒ wo wakimayenu hito, someone who cannot discern his bearings. The first letter is long ſ, correcting OCR f in the Portuguese continuation.

runs.text: He homem que eſtà alienado, ou como

lines.note: To gia completes hito ja, identifying such a person. The Portuguese calls him distracted or beside himself; the visible eſtà replaces the truncated OCR est.
Fora de si completes the figurative explanation of being beside oneself. It is the end of the preceding Tofǒ example.

runs.text: Esta parte, ou os da noßa parte. Pala-

lines.note: Tǒfǒ here denotes this side or one’s own party. The Portuguese narrows it to a military expression in the continuation; both long-o marks are carons.

runs.text: ura que ſe vſa na guerra.

lines.note: Completes palavra and states that this usage belongs to warfare. The short line is a usage restriction on Tǒfǒ, not an independent gloss.
Tǒfon is explained as sakasama ni taoruru, falling headfirst or overturned. Its literal physical sense is followed below by a metaphorical one.

runs.text: uirado, ou com a cabeça pera baixo. ¶ Item,

lines.note: Completes revirado and specifies falling with the head downward. Item introduces an additional figurative application.

runs.text: per met. O cair como da virtude, ou de ſua pro

lines.note: The metaphorical sense is falling away from virtue or from one’s professed rule. The visibly undivided ending pro continues as profissão; no line-end hyphen is supplied.
Completes profissão and adds one’s law or religion. The final upright S. is the dictionary’s written-register label, outside the italic gloss.

runs.text: Modo de estar ſolitario, ſem fazer

lines.note: Unaccented Tofon describes remaining solitary and inactive. The scan supports ſolitario, correcting OCR ſalitario; it is distinct from accented Tǒfon above.
Tofonto shite iru illustrates being in that inactive state. The Portuguese begins a comparison with someone standing stupefied.
Completes the inactive-state example as being stupefied without doing anything. The long-s spelling in paſmado is retained.

runs.text: Certa laya de comer que ſe faz de grãos

lines.note: Tǒfu is the food made from ground beans or grains and compared below with fresh cheese. The verb is faz, correcting OCR fuz; the gloss itself supplies the food identification.

runs.text: moidos à maneira de queijos freſcos.

lines.note: The ground material is prepared in the manner of fresh cheeses. This completes the comparison used to explain tofu, without making the food dairy-based.
Tǒfǔ here means the east wind, explained by higashi no kaze and kochi. The final letter is u with a caron, not OCR a; it distinguishes this wind entry from Tǒfu as food.
Leste completes vento Leste, east wind. The entire short continuation is Portuguese italic text.
Tǒfǔ and the alternative tǒfǔriǔ denote currently prevailing custom. The OCR’s extra a is the headword’s full stop; the following l is the Latin alternative marker.
Tǒfǔ ni shitagatte means following current custom. The u carries a caron in the example as well; the abbreviated Portuguese q̃ remains unexpanded.
The separately entered Tǒfǔriǔ refers back to the same prevailing-fashion sense. Both u-length marks are downward carons in this impression.

runs.text: Caſa onde ſe fazem, ou vendem a-

lines.note: Tǒfuya is the place where tofu is made or sold. The definition begins a reference back to the bean preparation compared with cheese.

runs.text: quella maneira de queijos feitos de grãos mol-

lines.note: Continues that comparison with cheese made from grains or beans. Mol- is visibly divided and continues into molles on the next row.
Completes molles nagoa: softened in water and ground. The printed contraction nagoa is retained as part of the tofu-making explanation.
Toga is sin or fault. Toga wo okasu gives the first construction, committing sins, whose Portuguese verb is divided Co-meter.
Completes cometer peccados and then gives toga wo yamuru, ceasing to sin. The second Portuguese verb continues as Ceſ-ſar below.

Completes the cessation example and introduces Togauo caiumuru, translated below as concealing or excusing sins. Enlargement shows a dotted i in caiumuru; this unusual literal reading is retained rather than silently replacing it with a contextually expected s-form.
Completes En-cobrir, concealing or excusing sins, and starts toga ni otsuru. The Portuguese noun reads peccados, correcting OCR peecados.
Votçuru completes toga ni otsuru, falling into sin. The following Togani begins the final example under the same headword.
Toga ni kiwamaru is rendered as being consummate or fully established in sins. The moral sense is supplied by the Portuguese, while the Japanese spelling is kept diplomatic.
Tǒgacu is glossed by ima no gakumon, present-day learning. The Portuguese equivalently gives current study, continued on the last row.
Ou dagora completes the contrast as study of the present time. This is the last body row in the first column and is not a catchword.

runs.text: Cerca, ou muro q̃ ſe faz ao derre-

lines.note: Togamaye is an enclosure or wall surrounding a fortified or royal place. Derre- starts the Portuguese expression for around, continued on the next row.

runs.text: dor da fortaleza, ou dos paços reaes, &c.

lines.note: Completes derredor and identifies the places enclosed as a fortress or royal palaces. This is the continuation of the construction term Togamaye.
Togame, togameru, togameta describes questioning someone with disapproval. The Portuguese comparison with reprimanding continues after co-.
Completes como quem reprende, as one who reproves. Notar introduces the related act of censuring; the OCR’s word break in Notar is not printed.
Reprender completes the additional sense of reproving or reprimanding. The printed word is continuous, correcting OCR re prender.
The noun Togame denotes reproof or censure, paired with the preceding verb. Nota here belongs to that moral or critical sense.
Tôgan is the eastern bank or shore, explained as higashi no kishi. The Portuguese describes elevated land on the east side; the long-o mark is a circumflex.
The example Tôgan seigan no yanagi juxtaposes eastern and western banks. Ya- begins yanagi, the willows named on the next row.

runs.text: Salgueiros da parte do Leſte, & Oeſte.

lines.note: Nagui completes yanagi. The Portuguese explicitly gives willows on the east and west sides; the last direction is Oeſte with capital O, correcting OCR Deſte.
Toganin denotes a sinner or person at fault. The internal n, rather than OCR u, is supported by the scan and the preceding toga entries.
Togaracaxi is making something pointed or sharp at the tip. Agu- begins agudo, completed below.
Completes agudo na ponta, sharp at the point. This specifies the result produced by Togaracaxi.
Togari is the intransitive counterpart, being sharp. Togatta begins an example with the past or resultative form before mono.

runs.text: Couſa de ponta aguda. ¶ Itẽ, per-

lines.note: Togatta mono is a thing with a sharp point. Item introduces a figurative description of a person, continued on the next row.

runs.text: met. Homem agaſtado, ou riſpido, & ſeuero

lines.note: The figurative sharp person is irritable, harsh, and severe. Met. completes per-met. from the preceding row and belongs to the Portuguese apparatus.
De condição completes the description of temperament. It explains a character trait, rather than the physical sharp point in the first sense.

runs.text: Sombreiro que tem bico agudo co-

lines.note: Togarigaſa is a hat with a pointed crown. The comparison introduced by co- continues with a Portuguese hat type below.
Completes como chapeo cuſcuſeiro, comparing the pointed hat with that named form. The historical Portuguese term is retained without substituting a modern hat classification.

runs.text: Frecha de ponta aguda, que logo ſe

lines.note: Togariya is an arrow with a sharp point. The following clause describes the widening shape behind that point.

runs.text: vai a largando, & fazendo como quadrada.

lines.note: The arrow broadens and becomes roughly square in form. The scan reads como quadrada, correcting OCR come quadra da; the printed a largando spacing is retained.

This Tǒgaſa is glossed as boubas, the disease term, distinct from the hat homonym below. The capital B is abraded; its surviving stem and bowls, together with the lexical context, support Boubas rather than OCR Coubas.
A separate Tǒgaſa denotes a Chinese hat. The neighboring disease entry must not be merged with this homonym merely because their Japanese forms match.
Togavocuri is satisfaction or atonement for sins. The Portuguese supplies a religious sense for a term built around toga, fault or sin.
Togayeri describes a falcon changing its feathers, that is, moulting. To- begins the accompanying Japanese example.
Togayeru taka is a falcon that moults. The example and its Portuguese translation complete the falconry entry.

runs.text: Cume do monte, ou alto da ladeira tè

lines.note: Togue is the mountain summit or the top of a pass reached before descending. The o’s upper edge is abraded and no secure complete accent is established, so the unmarked baseline is retained. The supplied NINJAL index lists Tǒgue (259b14); that lexical checkpoint does not establish the mark in this impression. Reference: NINJAL, Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, version 202510, CC BY 4.0, https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html.

runs.text: onde ſobem, & donde tornão a decer.

lines.note: Explains the top as the point up to which people climb and from which they descend again. This completes the geographical definition of Togue.
Togue, toguru, togeta introduces achieving, fulfilling, or enjoying something. Fõ- begins the first example, honmō, a cherished wish, on the next row.
Fõmǒ wo toguru means fulfilling one’s wishes. Sã- begins the next Japanese example and is wholly roman, correcting the OCR’s accidental italic S.

Sãjǒ wo togue describes paying someone a visit; S. is the upright written-register label. The Portuguese ending appears to contain an extra c in viſitãdco after the d. This irregular printed form is retained provisionally rather than silently normalized to viſitãdo.

Muron wo toguru is explained as succeeding with treason or carrying it out. Muronuo is retained as the visible form, though the traitorous sense would suggest the familiar muhon; the weak r is not replaced solely from that expectation.
Completes the treason example as putting it into effect. Ten no yorokobi wo toguru begins the next example, enjoying heavenly joys.
Guru completes toguru and the Portuguese explicitly gives enjoying celestial joys. This closes the sequence of different objects and senses under Togue.
Tôguet means the winter moon, explained by fuyu no tsuki. Final S. is upright and labels the written expression; the circumflex over o is retained.

runs.text: O que tem por officioalimpar, & aſa-

lines.note: Togui here is the professional who cleans and polishes blades. The scan supports officioalimpar, restoring the missing f and c while retaining the unusually close printed boundary before alimpar.
Completes aſa-calar, polishing or burnishing swords. The noun is eſpadas, correcting the OCR vowel in eſpedas.
Togui, togu, toida is sharpening or polishing a blade. The Portuguese aſacalar and amolar distinguish the associated actions without changing the Japanese principal parts.

Completes eſpadas and adds Catanas as another name for the blades. Catanas is the Japanese-derived blade name embedded in the Portuguese explanation; its observed italic type is retained and the whole term is listed for optional human font review.

runs.text: Companhia, que faz hum ao outro por

lines.note: A separate Togui denotes companionship provided by one person to another. The following row explains its purpose and gives a Japanese example.
Hito no togi ni naru is keeping someone company so that he is not alone. The Portuguese Acõ- starts acompanhar and is wholly italic, unlike the OCR’s split font treatment.
Completes acompanhar as accompanying someone in this manner. It closes the companionship entry rather than the sharpening entries above.
Tǒguin denotes the present sovereign, described as the king of now or of this age. The close spacing in deſtaidade is retained.
Toguiya is the place where blades are cleaned and polished. The plural verbs describe the workshop’s activity, whose object follows below.
As eſpadas supplies the swords as the object of cleaning and polishing. This genuine short continuation belongs to Toguiya.
Togǒ is equated with fude, a Japanese writing brush. Togǒ- begins the example concerning the limits of putting something into writing.

runs.text: Não ha pera q̃ mais eſcreuer.

lines.note: Togǒ ni atawazu is rendered as there being no need to write further. The abbreviation q̃ remains unexpanded, and the final written-register label S. is upright.
Tǒgocu denotes this kingdom. The scan’s downward caron corrects the OCR circumflex; the separate catchword below repeats the form as page furniture.
